doc.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Best pianists today: Oscar Peterson, Hyman, Nero, Roger Williams
summary: He names Oscar Peterson the best jazz pianist, Dick Hyman the best all-round, and praises Nero and Roger Williams.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: That’s the only way you go. I mean there’s always somebody that’s going to play a hell of a lot more than you do. Like today, to me the best jazz pianist going today is Oscar. Bar none. I don’t make any exceptions with that. That’s with jazz. For the best all around pianist I think is Dick Hyman, who has all the bases covered. And then Peter Nero is excellent, Roger Williams for what Roger does I think is great. Because I don’t think Roger was a natural, Roger had to practice one heck of a lot to play the way he plays, to get to where he got, it took a lot of work, but he got there. And he’s gotten better and better as he’s gone along. He cut away from the vanilla chords. He sent me an album of his one time “On A Clear Day,” and I just tell him, my God, you know the harmonic thing was such a change from “Autumn Leaves” and the kind of commercial things he did you know. He was very successful commercially, in other words I mean his harmonic changes, which don’t really mean too much to the general public — you can play four © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
